result.title: Top Cybersecurity Risks & Tackling Forever Chemicals | WEF | Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:14 - How air bubbles filter forever chemicals: PFAS, or ‘forever chemicals’ are found in masses of products, from non-stick pans to clothing. US company Allonnia provides a solution to remove PFAS from water using a simple resource: air. Allonnia is a World Economic Forum Global Innovator, part of a community of promising growth-stage companies at the forefront of disruption and innovation in their industries. PFAS destruction technologies have been selected as one of the World Economic Forum’s Top 10 Emerging Technologies of 2026. 


03.21 - The biggest cybersecurity risks today: Five experts from across the #cybersecurity sector highlight the most pressing threats, and how we should respond: Kemba Walden, President of the Paladin Global Institute and Former US Acting National Cyber Director; Amy Hogan-Burney, Deputy CISO, Governance and Risk at Microsoft; Haley van Loon, CEO of Crime Stoppers International; Marc van Zadelhoff, CEO of Mimecast; and Kat Duffy, Senior Fellow for Digital and CyberspacePolicy at the Council on Foreign Relations.


06.46 - Top HR exec advice for new graduates: This year’s graduates are entering a very different workplace from their predecessors. As employers integrate AI across organizations, the market for entry-level jobs is changing fast. How can #graduates prepare for this fast-changing world? Carina Cortez, Chief People Officer at AI-workforce platform Cornerstone On Demand, and Maria Flynn, President and CEO of Jobs For The Future, share their insights.

result.title: Ideas on the Move: Quarraisha Abdool Karim
result.description:
"As scientists, we've brought hope. We've brought the tools."

Dr Quarraisha Abdool Karim is one of the world's leading HIV scientists. She joined us in Dalian with a clear-eyed view of where the fight stands today.

The science has delivered: a promising new twice-yearly injectable that could be a genuine game-changer for young women. But the risk of HIV slipping off the global agenda remains, as funding shifts and multilateralism faces new pressure.

Her message is direct: ending AIDS as a public health threat now requires a whole-of-society approach - government, civil society and industry working together, to get these lifesaving tools to the people who need them.

#AMNC26 #IdeasOnTheMove

result.title: Ideas on the Move: Ma Yansong
result.description:
"I'm an architect, so I build dreams."

When Ma Yansong joined us in Dalian as a Cultural Leader,, he shared a philosophy on design that goes far beyond function. For him, the built environment should inspire and connect us.

Growing up in Beijing, he discovered that nature could be emotional, dramatic – even spiritual. That belief shapes everything he builds: not just adding trees to a skyline, but creating genuine emotional connection to place.

He points to traditional Japanese dry gardens as the model - sand and stones that somehow evoke the ocean, the islands, the universe. That imaginative space, he says, is exactly what today's cities are missing.

#IdeasOnTheMove #AMNC26

result.title: What is a Digital Embassy?
result.description:
Every country wants a stake in AI. Few have the infrastructure to compete alone. Digital embassies solve this: a country can have its digital systems hosted abroad, while having them governed by its own laws. 

The result: AI capability without giving up sovereignty.

Learn more in our recent white paper: https://www.weforum.org/publications/ai-infrastructure-in-the-age-of-sovereignty-requirements-strategies-and-a-trusted-framework-for-digital-embassies/
